name: Abū al-Qāsim ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khathʿamī al-Suhaylī
summary: Blind Andalusian scholar of Málaga, author of a famous commentary on the Prophet's biography and of Natāʾij al-fikr, a book of original views in grammar.
bio: Al-Suhaylī was born near Málaga in 508/1114 and lost his sight at seventeen. He taught in Málaga until the Almohad caliph called him to Marrakesh, where he died in 581/1185. His al-Rawḍ al-unuf, a commentary on Ibn Hishām's biography of the Prophet, is his best-known work.

In grammar his Natāʾij al-fikr and his dictated notes argue questions afresh, often against the received Basran answers, and later grammarians, Ibn Mālik and Abū Ḥayyān among them, quote 'al-Suhaylī' as a voice of his own.

sources.title: Süheylî, Abdurrahman b. Abdullah, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
